Gramlot 0.2.15 completes the `auth` side of the 0.2.14 contract: a Source element whose `auth` rule the server refuses never reaches the client.

## What changes

- `auth="rule"` on an element of `main` or of a `@source` fragment: when the server serialises the fragment, an element whose rule the evaluator refuses is left out with its subtree; an accepted element is sent without its `auth` attribute (the rule belongs to the server). `GramlotBuilder(auth=…)` / `{auth}` receives the evaluator from `GramlotServer`; `GramlotBuilder.to_tytx()` (new, the counterpart of `toTytx()`) serialises `GramlotBuilderBag.authorized_copy(auth)` / `authorizedCopy(auth)`. A non-string rule answers `application_error`. The base server refuses every rule (`not_authenticated`); a server with the `auth` capability evaluates it (gramlot-py-server 0.2.7 on Kajenn). Closes gramlot-org/gramlot#34.
- Conformance: item 15 of GC-230 §150 checks that a refused element is absent from `check_fragment_auth`; the former items 15 and 16 are 16 and 17.
- Docs: GC-230 §030 states the element rule with its citations; GC-095 §100 documents `auth` on elements; the sentence saying that Source methods were not yet part of the page-writing API is replaced (fragments and endpoints are declared; only the declarative `remote` attribute is still deferred).

## Upgrading from 0.2.14

- Pages: nothing to change. A page that relied on reading the `auth` attribute in the browser no longer sees it.
- Adapters: nothing to change; conformance fixtures gain `check_fragment_auth`, as the core fixtures do.
